headline: US Mortgage Rates Ease to 7.32% in First Pullback Since August
summary: The benchmark 30-year fixed-rate mortgage in the U.S. dropped to 7.32% from 7.40% amid a bond market rally that pushed the 10-year Treasury yield toward its biggest drop in two years.
why: Mortgage rates directly affect housing affordability and real estate sector activity, with bond market yields serving as the primary pricing benchmark for home loans.

impacts.name: Real Estate
impacts.why: A decline in benchmark borrowing costs offers slight relief to prospective homebuyers facing elevated interest rates.

why_moved: A sharp rally in government bonds reduced benchmark yields, prompting a corresponding easing in retail mortgage rates.
